verses.zh: 大卫数点跟随他的人，立千夫长、百夫长率领他们。
verses.en: David assembled the army that was with him. He appointed leaders of thousands and leaders of hundreds.

verses.zh: 大卫打发军兵出战，分为三队：一队在约押手下，一队在洗鲁雅的儿子、约押兄弟亚比筛手下，一队在迦特人以太手下。大卫对军兵说：「我必与你们一同出战。」
verses.en: David then sent out the army—a third under the leadership of Joab, a third under the leadership of Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under the leadership of Ittai the Gittite. The king said to the troops, “I too will indeed march out with you.”

verses.zh: 军兵却说：「你不可出战。若是我们逃跑，敌人必不介意；我们阵亡一半，敌人也不介意。因为你一人强似我们万人，你不如在城里预备帮助我们。」
verses.en: But the soldiers replied,[NOTE:1] “You should not do this![NOTE:2] For if we should have to make a rapid retreat, they won’t be concerned about us.[NOTE:3] Even if half of us should die, they won’t be concerned. But you[NOTE:4] are like 10,000 of us! So it is better if you remain in the city for support.”
notes: Heb “the people said.”
Heb “march out.”
Heb “they will not place to us heart.”
The translation follows the LXX (except for the Lucianic recension), Symmachus, and Vulgate in reading אָתָּה (ʾattah, “you”) rather than MT עָתָּה (ʿattah, “now”).

verses.zh: 王向他们说：「你们以为怎样好，我就怎样行。」于是王站在城门旁，军兵或百或千地挨次出去了。
verses.en: Then the king said to them, “I will do whatever seems best to you.”So the king stayed beside the city gate, while all the army marched out by hundreds and by thousands.

verses.zh: 王嘱咐约押、亚比筛、以太说：「你们要为我的缘故宽待那少年人押沙龙。」王为押沙龙嘱咐众将的话，兵都听见了。
verses.en: The king gave this order to Joab, Abishai, and Ittai: “For my sake deal gently with the young man Absalom.” Now the entire army was listening when the king gave all the leaders this order concerning Absalom.

verses.zh: 兵就出到田野迎着以色列人，在以法莲树林里交战。
verses.en: Then the army marched out to the field to fight against Israel. The battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.

verses.zh: 以色列人败在大卫的仆人面前；那日阵亡的甚多，共有二万人。
verses.en: The army of Israel was defeated there by David’s men.[NOTE:1] The slaughter there was great that day—20,000 soldiers were killed.
notes: Heb “servants” (also in v. 9).

verses.zh: 因为在那里四面打仗，死于树林的比死于刀剑的更多。
verses.en: The battle there was spread out over the whole area, and the forest consumed more soldiers than the sword devoured that day.

verses.zh: 押沙龙偶然遇见大卫的仆人。押沙龙骑着骡子，从大橡树密枝底下经过，他的头发被树枝绕住，就悬挂起来，所骑的骡子便离他去了。
verses.en: Then Absalom happened to come across David’s men. Now as Absalom was riding on his[NOTE:1] mule, it[NOTE:2] went under the branches of a large oak tree. His head got caught in the oak and he was suspended in midair,[NOTE:3] while the mule he had been riding kept going.
notes: Heb “the.”
Heb “the donkey.”
Heb “between the sky and the ground.”

verses.zh: 有个人看见，就告诉约押说：「我看见押沙龙挂在橡树上了。」
verses.en: When one[NOTE:1] of the men saw this, he reported it to Joab saying, “I saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree.”
notes: 4QSama lacks the word “one.”

verses.zh: 约押对报信的人说：「你既看见他，为甚么不将他打死落在地上呢？你若打死他，我就赏你十舍客勒银子，一条带子。」
verses.en: Joab replied to the man who was telling him this, “What! You saw this? Why didn’t you strike him down right on the spot?[NOTE:1] I would have given you 10 pieces of silver[NOTE:2] and a commemorative belt!”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Why did you not strike him down there to the ground.”
Heb “10 [shekels] of silver.” This would have been about 4 ounces (114 grams) of silver by weight.
Heb “and a girdle” (so KJV); NIV “a warrior’s belt”; CEV “a special belt”; NLT “a hero’s belt.”

verses.zh: 那人对约押说：「我就是得你一千舍客勒银子，我也不敢伸手害王的儿子；因为我们听见王嘱咐你和亚比筛并以太说：『你们要谨慎，不可害那少年人押沙龙。』
verses.en: The man replied to Joab, “Even if[NOTE:1] I were receiving[NOTE:2] 1,000 pieces of silver,[NOTE:3] I would not strike[NOTE:4] the king’s son! In our very presence[NOTE:5] the king gave this order to you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.’[NOTE:6]
notes: The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading וְלוּ (velu, “and if”) rather than MT וְלֹא (velo’, “and not”).
Heb “weighing out in my hand.”
Heb “a thousand [shekels] of silver.” This would have been about 25 pounds (11.4 kg) of silver by weight.
Heb “extend my hand against.”
Heb “in our ears.”

The Hebrew text is very difficult here. The MT reads מִי (mi, “who”), apparently yielding the following sense: “Show care, whoever you might be, for the youth Absalom.” The Syriac Peshitta reads li (“for me”), the Hebrew counterpart of which may also lie behind the LXX rendering μοι (moi, “for me”). This reading seems preferable here, since it restores sense to the passage and most easily explains the rise of the variant.

verses.zh: 我若妄为害了他的性命，就是你自己也必与我为敌（原来，无论何事都瞒不过王。）」
verses.en: If I had acted at risk of my own life[NOTE:1]—and nothing is hidden from the king—you would have abandoned me.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The translation follows the Qere, many medieval Hebrew mss, and a number of the ancient versions in reading בְנַפְשִׁי (venafshi, “against my life”) rather than the MT בְנַפְשׁוֹ (venafsho, “against his life”).
Heb “stood aloof.”

verses.zh: 约押说：「我不能与你留连。」约押手拿三杆短枪，趁押沙龙在橡树上还活着，就刺透他的心。
verses.en: Joab replied, “I will not wait around like this for you!” He took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the middle of Absalom while he was still alive in the middle of the oak tree.[NOTE:1]
notes: There is a play on the word “heart” here that is difficult to reproduce in English. Literally the Hebrew text says “he took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the heart of the oak tree.” This figure of speech involves the use of the same word in different senses and is known as antanaclasis. It is illustrated in the familiar saying from the time of the American Revolution: “If we don’t hang together, we will all hang separately.” The present translation understands “heart” to be used somewhat figuratively for “chest” (cf. TEV, CEV), which explains why Joab’s armor-bearers could still “kill” Absalom after he had been stabbed with three spears through the “heart.” Since trees do not have “chests” either, the translation uses “middle.”

verses.zh: 给约押拿兵器的十个少年人围绕押沙龙，将他杀死。
verses.en: Then 10 soldiers who were Joab’s armor-bearers struck Absalom and finished him off.

verses.zh: 约押吹角，拦阻众人，他们就回来，不再追赶以色列人。
verses.en: Then Joab blew the trumpet[NOTE:1] and the army turned back from chasing Israel, for Joab had called for the army to halt.
notes: Heb “the shofar” (the ram’s horn trumpet).

verses.zh: 他们将押沙龙丢在林中一个大坑里，上头堆起一大堆石头。以色列众人都逃跑，各回各家去了。
verses.en: They took Absalom, threw him into a large pit in the forest, and stacked a huge pile of stones over him. In the meantime all the Israelite soldiers fled to their homes.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and all Israel fled, each to his tent.” In this context this refers to the supporters of Absalom (see vv. 6-7, 16).

verses.zh: 押沙龙活着的时候，在王谷立了一根石柱，因他说：「我没有儿子为我留名。」他就以自己的名称那石柱叫押沙龙柱，直到今日。
verses.en: Before this[NOTE:1] Absalom[NOTE:2] had set up a monument[NOTE:3] and dedicated it to himself in the King’s Valley, reasoning, “I have no son who will carry on my name.” He named the monument after himself, and to this day it is known as Absalom’s Memorial.
notes: Heb “and in his life.”
This disjunctive clause (conjunction + subject + verb) describes an occurrence that preceded the events just narrated.
Heb “a pillar.”

verses.zh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯说：「容我跑去，将耶和华向仇敌给王报仇的信息报与王知。」
verses.en: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Let me run and give the king the good news that the Lord has vindicated him before his enemies.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “that the Lord has vindicated him from the hand of his enemies.”

verses.zh: 约押对他说：「你今日不可去报信，改日可以报信；因为今日王的儿子死了，所以你不可去报信。」
verses.en: But Joab said to him, “You will not be a bearer of good news today. You will bear good news some other day, but not today,[NOTE:1] for the king’s son is dead.”
notes: Heb “but this day you will not bear good news.”

verses.zh: 约押对古示人说：「你去将你所看见的告诉王。」古示人在约押面前下拜，就跑去了。
verses.en: Then Joab said to the Cushite, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” After bowing to Joab, the Cushite ran off.

verses.zh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯又对约押说：「无论怎样，求你容我随着古示人跑去。」约押说：「我儿，你报这信息，既不得赏赐，何必要跑去呢？」
verses.en: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok again spoke to Joab, “Whatever happens, let me go after the Cushite.” But Joab said, “Why is it that you want to go, my son? You have no good news that will bring you a reward.”

verses.zh: 他又说：「无论怎样，我要跑去。」约押说：「你跑去吧！」亚希玛斯就从平原往前跑，跑过古示人去了。
verses.en: But he said,[NOTE:1] “Whatever happens, I want to go!” So Joab[NOTE:2] said to him, “Then go!” So Ahimaaz ran by the way of the Jordan plain, and he passed the Cushite.
notes: The words “but he said” are not in the Hebrew text. They are supplied in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he”; the referent (Joab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 大卫正坐在城瓮里。守望的人上城门楼的顶上，举目观看，见有一个人独自跑来。
verses.en: Now David was sitting between the inner and outer gates,[NOTE:1] and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate at the wall. When he looked, he saw a man running by himself.
notes: Heb “the two gates.”

verses.zh: 守望的人就大声告诉王。王说：「他若独自来，必是报口信的。」那人跑得渐渐近了。
verses.en: So the watchman called out and informed the king. The king said, “If he is by himself, he brings good news.”[NOTE:1] The runner[NOTE:2] came ever closer.
notes: Heb “good news is in his mouth.”
Heb “he”; the referent (the runner) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 守望的人又见一人跑来，就对守城门的人说：「又有一人独自跑来。」王说：「这也必是报信的。」
verses.en: Then the watchman saw another man running. The watchman called out to the gatekeeper, “There is another man running by himself.” The king said, “This one also is bringing good news.”

verses.zh: 守望的人说：「我看前头人的跑法，好像撒督的儿子亚希玛斯的跑法一样。」王说：「他是个好人，必是报好信息。」
verses.en: The watchman said, “It appears to me that the first runner is Ahimaaz[NOTE:1] son of Zadok.” The king said, “He is a good man, and he comes with good news.”
notes: Heb “I am seeing the running of the first one like the running of Ahimaaz.”

verses.zh: 亚希玛斯向王呼叫说：「平安了！」就在王面前脸伏于地叩拜，说：「耶和华―你的　神是应当称颂的，因他已将那举手攻击我主我王的人交给王了。」
verses.en: Then Ahimaaz called out and said to the king, “Greetings!”[NOTE:1] He bowed down before the king with his face toward the ground and said, “May the Lord your God be praised because he has defeated[NOTE:2] the men who opposed[NOTE:3] my lord the king!”
notes: Heb “Peace.”
Heb “delivered over.”
Heb “lifted their hand against.”

verses.zh: 王问说：「少年人押沙龙平安不平安？」亚希玛斯回答说：「约押打发王的仆人，那时仆人听见众民大声喧哗，却不知道是甚么事。」
verses.en: The king replied, “How is the young man Absalom?” Ahimaaz replied, “I saw a great deal of confusion when Joab was sending the king’s servant and me, your servant, but I don’t know what it was all about.”

verses.zh: 王说：「你退去，站在旁边。」他就退去，站在旁边。
verses.en: The king said, “Turn aside and take your place here.” So he turned aside and waited.

verses.zh: 古示人也来到，说：「有信息报给我主我王！耶和华今日向一切兴起攻击你的人给你报仇了。」
verses.en: Then the Cushite arrived and said,[NOTE:1] “May my lord the king now receive the good news! The Lord has vindicated you today and delivered you from the hand of all who have rebelled against you!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And look, the Cushite came and the Cushite said.”
Heb “for the Lord has vindicated you today from the hand of all those rising against you.”

verses.zh: 王问古示人说：「少年人押沙龙平安不平安？」古示人回答说：「愿我主我王的仇敌，和一切兴起要杀害你的人，都与那少年人一样。」
verses.en: The king asked the Cushite, “How is the young man Absalom?” The Cushite replied, “May the enemies of my lord the king and all who have plotted against you[NOTE:1] be like that young man!”
notes: Heb “and all those rising against you for evil.”

verses.zh: 王就心里伤恸，上城门楼去哀哭，一面走一面说：「我儿押沙龙啊！我儿，我儿押沙龙啊！我恨不得替你死，押沙龙啊，我儿！我儿！」
verses.en: (19:1)[NOTE:1] The king then became very upset. He went up to the upper room over the gate and wept. As he went he said, “My son, Absalom! My son, my son,[NOTE:2] Absalom! If only I could have died in your place! Absalom, my son, my son!”[NOTE:3]
notes: This marks the beginning of ch. 19 in the Hebrew text. Beginning with 18:33, the verse numbers through 19:43 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 18:33 ET = 19:1 HT, 19:1 ET = 19:2 HT, 19:2 ET = 19:3 HT, etc., through 19:43 ET = 19:44 HT. From 20:1 the versification in the English Bible and the Hebrew Bible is again the same.
One medieval Hebrew ms, some mss of the LXX, and the Vulgate lack this repeated occurrence of “my son” due to haplography.
The Lucianic Greek recension and Syriac Peshitta lack this repeated occurrence of “my son” due to haplography.
